_note: REAL VALUES, confirmed 2026-09-02 from screenshots of the league's own ESPN 'Scoring Settings' screen (Intuitech Fantasy, 8 teams). Every category below was read directly off that screen. This league differs from league-1 in three structural ways: 4-point passing TDs (not 6), -1 per interception (not -2), and six FG distance bands (not three). It has NO yardage-milestone bonuses, NO defensive return-yardage category, and NO defensive yards-allowed tier -- all three are absent from the settings screen, which is why they are absent here rather than set to zero.
_absent_categories_note: Deliberately NOT present, because the ESPN screen does not list them: (a) def_return_yd -- no return-yardage line exists for D/ST in this league, (b) def_yards_allowed tiers -- only points-allowed bands are configured, (c) plain non-lost 'fumble' -- only 'Fumble Lost' (-2) appears, (d) yardage milestones for passing/rushing/receiving. An absent category contributes nothing, which is the correct behaviour here -- do not add them back with a value of 0 'for completeness', because that would misrepresent an unconfigured rule as a confirmed zero.
_points_allowed_note: The screen lists 0 / 1-6 / 7-13 / 14-20 / 28-34 / 35+. The 21-27 band is not shown, which is ESPN's convention for a band worth exactly 0 -- encoded here as {max: 27, points: 0} so the tier ladder stays continuous. Without that entry a 24-point game would fall through to the 28-34 band and be scored -1.
_unmapped_categories_note: Three categories below are real league rules with no nflreadpy data source, so they will always contribute 0 in practice: st_player_forced_fumble, st_player_fumble_rec (nflreadpy does not separate special-teams tackles from defensive ones at player level) and def_st_forced_fumble / def_st_fumble_rec (same, at team level). They are kept in the config because the rule exists and a future data source would make them live; each is worth 1 point and is vanishingly rare for a rostered fantasy player. This is the same graceful-miss contract every other category here uses.
